pattern.top_pattern: Unmapped facility values are creating a second validation gate
pattern.what_is_impacting: Medicaid facility classification in CO and IA
key_driver_codes: Other Disorders of Nervous System with MCC
pattern.pattern_details: Spend is rising in claims assigned to Not Mapped instead of a usable facility type in CO and IA. Because one market is mixed volume and unit cost while the other is mainly volume-led, the business issue cannot be called until the site-of-care mapping is fixed. This is a second validation gate separate from the AUTH code shifts.
pattern.why_it_matters: Unmapped facilities hide the true site of care and can misdirect both network and UM actions.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Map the underlying facilities behind Not Mapped claims in CO and IA and reroute confirmed spend to the correct site-of-care worklists.
pattern.validation_reason: Facility classification is incomplete, so the real provider and site-of-care signal is not yet reliable.
evidence_summary: CO Family Care / Not Mapped added +$0.5M with 24 more admissions and about +$19.3K paid per admit.
IA LTSS Dual Eligible / Not Mapped added +$0.4M with 49 more admissions while paid per admit fell about $2.8K.
Both markets carry unmapped or unknown facility flags, so the spend cannot be tied cleanly to a real care setting yet.
